conviction_note: Q3 2026 is not pre-released and the FY guide (8-11% cc product growth) cannot be met at its midpoint without a sharp H2 slowdown, so a nudge up or narrowing is the most likely new line. That is the one positive finding. Against it: the US is visibly decelerating, the disputed USD 4.4m Asieris receivable is still on the balance sheet, and the new CFO is a capital-raising banker joining with NOK 162m of cash. The last guide raise (Q2) was sold -4.75%. The findings net to about +0.1, so p_up sits at 50 and expected_move is 0, while abs_move stays at 6 because the numbers and possibly the guide are new.

new_in_release.expect: Hexvix/Cysview revenue around NOK 136-139m (Q3 2025: 134.1m). That is high-single-digit cc growth translated at USD/NOK -5.8% and EUR/NOK -7.3% YoY, so roughly +1-4% reported in NOK. Direction against the unsourced bar is unknown.
Upward narrowing or a raise of the 8-11% cc range is more likely than a cut, because H1 ran at +14% cc and the guide's midpoint implies H2 at about +5% cc
Asieris arbitration: either a status update or a provision against the USD 4.4m receivable. No settlement had been released as inside information by 27 Oct.
Cash below NOK 162m: Vesica integration costs and earn-out/Ipsen payments, against positive core EBITDA. Unknown magnitude.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide of 8-11% cc product revenue growth, set against H1 2026 at +14% cc (Q1 +18%, Q2 +11%), implies H2 growth of only about +2% to +8% cc. A Q3 near Q2's trend therefore makes an upward narrowing or raise the likeliest guidance action in the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 raised the low end (7-11% to 8-11%) and the stock fell 4.75%. Q3 2025 narrowed 7-11% to 8-10% and the stock rose 1.68%. Upward guide changes have not been rewarded reliably.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic (FY2025 H/C NOK 530.8m; H1 2026 +14% cc; guide 8-11%) is not written anywhere the search found, and no Q3 preview or consensus surfaced in English or Norwegian. If the market were positioned for a raise, the stock would have rerated from the ~48-50 range it has held since August, and the 20d run-up is -0.9%.
findings.independence: The deceleration data (NA cc growth 26% to 12%, US tower installs 11 to 6) point the other way and explain why the company may be keeping the range: https://cms.photocure.com/uploads/PHO_Q1_2026_ER_5a487caa27.pdf

findings.finding: US momentum is slowing into a tough comparison. North America cc growth fell from 26% in Q1 to 12% in Q2, new Saphira tower installs went 14 (Q3 2025), 11 (Q1 2026), 6 (Q2 2026), and active-account growth went 23% to 21% to 20%. Q3 2026 FX is a 5.8% (USD/NOK) and 7.3% (EUR/NOK) headwind, so the reported NOK headline will look like low single-digit growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: reported +3% (+11% cc), adjusted EBITDA flat, stock -4.75%. Q1 2025 and Q4 2024 prints fell 4.6% and 7.9%. Headline growth disappointments have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the deceleration and FX are public and sit inside what the company guided. What is left is the headline NOK print against a strong Q3 2025 comparison (14 towers, ForTec +6). FX averages computed from Yahoo NOK=X and EURNOK=X for Jul-Sep 2025 vs Jul-Sep 2026.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 release for the comparison base (H/C NOK 134.1m, 14 towers): https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=658171

findings.finding: Of the USD 13m in milestones recognised as revenue in Q1 2026, USD 8.6m was collected (USD 6.6m China partial, USD 2.0m EU MAA in full). That leaves about USD 4.4m (~NOK 42m, ~3% of market cap) receivable, which Asieris's 3 Aug counterclaim disputes in full. With no settlement released as inside information by 27 Oct, the Q3 report is more likely to carry a provision or a 'discussions ongoing' update than a resolution, even though the Theramex deal needs Asieris to align with the upstream licence.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 4 Aug 2026 (counterclaim announced, inside information) the stock was around 48.5 and insiders bought at 48.48-48.70 three days later. No results-day precedent for a provision.
findings.why_not_priced: The dispute is public, but nothing tells the market whether the receivable will be impaired in Q3. Adjusted EBITDA excludes milestones, so a provision would hit reported EBIT/net and the balance sheet, not the guided metric. A one-off below the guided line is sized at a fraction of the money. If a settlement were priced, the Theramex deal (7 Oct) would have lifted the stock, and it did not (48.7-49.5).
findings.independence: Q2 2026 report Note 4 and accounts receivable NOK 124.9m vs 73.1m PY: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=678772 ; Asieris counterclaim: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=679001

findings.finding: The new CFO (effective 26 Oct) is a 25-year healthcare investment banker whose stated expertise is 'capital raising, M&A, restructuring'. He joins with cash at NOK 162.4m (down from 239m a year earlier) and long-term earn-out liabilities of NOK 88.0m (Ipsen) plus NOK 88.5m (Vesica) while AssureMDx is pre-revenue until 2027. The release may therefore carry financing or strategic language. What the money would buy is a commercial-stage diagnostic launch, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent in the reaction history: Photocure has not raised equity in the observed window.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference. The CFO appointment drew no price reaction (49.3 to 49.0), so the market has not read it as a financing signal. If it had, the stock would sit below its August insider-buy level of ~48.5, and it does not. Kept small because the core business is EBITDA-positive and the money would fund a ramp.
findings.independence: Cash and earn-out liabilities in the Q2 2026 report: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=678772

baseline_tension: Little tension. The lean (+0.045) and run-up (-0.9% 20d) are flat, and the findings net to about zero: a likely guide nudge up against a US slowdown, an Asieris provision risk and a financing-flavoured CFO hire.
language_note: NewsWeb filings are English-only for this issuer (category labels are bilingual), so the filing half added nothing language-specific.

The Nordnet Norwegian retail forum carried three items not found in English sources: a takeover valuation by Lau Svenssen (NOK 120-150), a claim of ~NOK 100m Cevira China sales, and an undated 'ABG kutter Photocure-kursmål til NOK 70' headline. None was verifiable, so none is load-bearing.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' (guidance change, median move 9.0%): abs_move_pct 5.0 -> 6.0; the guidance finding +0.8 -> +1.0.
'A finding about what the market was told is worth ~0' and 'inside the guide': the US deceleration/FX reported-quarter finding -0.6 -> -0.3.
'A one-off below the guided line is sized at a fraction': the Asieris receivable provision -0.4 -> -0.3, since adjusted EBITDA excludes milestones.
Net findings moved from -0.5 to +0.1, and with the Q2 guide raise sold, p_up 48 -> 50, so expected_move_pct -0.2 -> 0.0.
